ShortDescription.Value: Close the median at a junction, built or painted: the median or center line runs through, crossing turns are removed and the crosswalks stay.

Publish.LongDescription:
Close the opening in a divided road's built-in median at a junction, so a side street can only turn in and out on its own side (right-in, right-out with right-hand traffic). The junction keeps the road's own median, curbs and crosswalks, and vehicles can no longer cross it.
On a road with a painted center line instead of a built median, closing the junction continues the line through it and removes the same turns.
**What it does** - Draws the road's own median through the junction, with its curbs and surface. - On a road with a painted center line, continues the line through the junction in the same colour and style instead. Nothing is built. - Takes every car turn that crosses the closed median out of the route network. The game's turn signs only make a turn more expensive, so vehicles would otherwise still take it now and then. Vehicles planning such a turn find another route; a vehicle already in the turn finishes it. - Keeps the crosswalks across the divided road, one on each carriageway, ending at the median. With traffic lights, pedestrians keep their crossing phase. - Continues the lines beside the median through the junction in the same colour and style, where the approaches have them (The Curbside Mod draws them). - At a T-junction whose side street is a divided road too, the through road's median closes and the side street keeps its own median end. - Reopening gives the junction back as it was.
**How to use** 1. Forbid every movement across the median or center line first: the turns in and out across it (left turns with right-hand traffic, right turns with left-hand traffic) and, at a crossroads, straight ahead from the side streets. Use the game's turn signs or Traffic's lane connector. The tool draws the movements still allowed in red. Rules made with Traffic's lane connector last only while Traffic is loaded, and a road upgrade can reset them; the game's turn signs need no other mod. 2. Click the round blue median button in the top-left row of mod buttons, or press F8. 3. Point at a junction. Blue: it can be closed. Orange: it is closed (click to reopen). Red: it cannot be closed yet, and the panel says why. Grey: there is nothing to close, or a painted road there does not qualify (the panel says why). Left-click to close or reopen; right-click or F8 leaves the tool.
A newly closed median is drawn once the vehicles already in a crossing turn have left the junction (at most about 30 seconds of game time).
**Supported** - Junctions where the two approaches of the divided road use the same road type and the same physical divider, including gently curved roads and the game's grass upgrade. - Two-way roads with a painted center line, single or double, the game's own or The Curbside Mod's, at T-junctions and crossroads, where both sides of the junction are the same road type. Where two painted roads cross, only the wider one can be closed; if it does not qualify, the junction cannot be closed. - A painted strip between the directions with a line along each edge, for example a Road Builder road with an empty lane in the middle and The Curbside Mod's lines along it. Without The Curbside Mod the game draws one center line in a strip up to about 1.5 m wide and no line along a wider one, so a wider strip cannot be closed. - Right-hand and left-hand traffic. - Tested with Traffic, Traffic Tool Essentials, Road Builder, Driveway Entries and The Curbside Mod loaded, and with this mod alone. Painted medians were tested with The Curbside Mod's double center line, the game's own single center line without The Curbside Mod, a Road Builder road, a 2 m painted strip built with Road Builder (with The Curbside Mod's lines along it), a curve of about 40 m radius and a crossroads. Built and painted medians were both tested with left-hand traffic.
**Not supported** - Roundabouts, level crossings, tram or train tracks, paths joining the junction, tunnels, elevated roads and middle platforms. - Crossroads where both roads are divided, crossroads of two painted roads of the same width, and junctions where more than four roads meet. - One-way roads, and roads with no line between their directions. - A road, divided or painted, that bends more than about 11 degrees or is steeper than about 8% at the junction, or whose two sides at the junction are more than 1 m apart in height; and roads with two medians.
**Saves** - Closures are saved with the city. - Changing the roads at a closed junction so that it no longer qualifies (for example building a divided road on the fourth arm of a T closed on a divided road) reopens it. Close it again once it qualifies. Replacing a closed junction's road with the other kind, divided for painted or painted for divided, also reopens it. - A new road on the fourth arm of a closed T keeps the closure when the new road is undivided or the closed road is painted, and its movements across the median are removed at once. A built median is not drawn until those movements are forbidden; a painted line stays drawn. - A closure on roads that another mod provides, such as Road Builder, stays closed to traffic while the city is loaded without that mod, but nothing is drawn there; once the mod is back it is drawn again, also if the city was saved in between. If the junction does not qualify without the mod, it is released, and a city saved then keeps it open. - Removing this mod is safe: the city loads and the closed junctions are ordinary open junctions again. A city saved while the mod was removed keeps those junctions open when the mod is back. Bus lines that were re-routed around a closed median keep that route until the line is edited. - The removed turns are not saved; the game rebuilds its route network on every load and the mod removes them again.
**Known limits** - Where the road's own median does not fit between the through lanes, for example where the two approaches are sharply offset, the junction stays closed to traffic but keeps its regular road surface. The tool's panel says why. - If a turn across a closed median is allowed again (for example after Traffic is removed, or after a road upgrade resets Traffic's lane connections), the mod still keeps that turn out of the route network, but the median is not drawn and the panel shows "Closed to traffic, median not drawn". On a painted median the line stays drawn and the panel still says "Painted median closed". Forbid the turn again, preferably with the game's turn signs. - A closed painted median stays closed to traffic if its center line is removed later or both sides of the road are replaced by a type without one. Nothing is drawn across the junction then, but the panel still says "Painted median closed"; reopen it with the tool. - Road Builder roads: at the one divided Road Builder junction tried, the median did not fit between the lanes, so it is closed to traffic but its median is not drawn. Both sides of a junction must be the same Road Builder road: a segment changed on its own in Road Builder becomes a road type of its own, and the panel then says the two sides are different road types. Place the road with Road Builder's Place More instead. - Not tested yet: medians wider than 5 m, the tree upgrade, a divided side street that leaves as a bridge, The Curbside Mod's invisible crosswalks, and painted strips wider than 2 m.
Built for game version 1.6.4f1.
Source code for this release is available on [GitHub](https://github.com/dexter-adams/conditional-medians).

ChangeLog.Value: Painted strips: the lines along a painted strip between the directions are now found with more room to spare, so a strip whose lines sit a little further into the lanes is not refused. Tested with left-hand traffic, Road Builder roads, a 2 m painted strip, and replacing a closed junction's road with the other kind.
